title: Just released a demo for my game Stompworks
author: Mekkablood
selftext:
This is a Roguelike where you you customize your mech by buying more parts as you go along. The skins you get are retained post death. Faster gameplay than most mech games outside of Armored Core, but feels like a faster version of a more traditional mech game in movement. [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5383780/Stompworks/?beta=0](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5383780/Stompworks/?beta=0)

Was done in Opus 5.5, no mcp's just prompting directly what I wanted. Starting very small focusing on models first, then branching out into the levels and gameplay. It was a small books worth of prompts to get to this.

comments.author: AccomplishedSugar790
comments.body: It looks fun. I like AI gamedev but I am allergic at this point to the ping pong ding pyong bell placeholder synthed sounds as a substitute for actual sound effects. You can get tons of free sounds from [freesound.org](http://freesound.org) and other resources, this game needs audio more than anything to get past that first impression.

replies.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
replies.body: Audio is a huge part of good gameplay. I've lost count of the amount of hours I've spent picking the right audio in the game I'm working on. From something as simple as a character pressing a button to explosions, doors opening, background music. It's an insane amount of work that most people don't even consider
